'''''Daihua sanqiong''''' is a possible ancestor of [[comb jellies]].<ref name="laura-geggel-2019a">{{Cite web |author1=Laura Geggel |date=2019-03-22 |title=520-Million-Year-Old Sea Monster Had 18 Mouth Tentacles |url=https://www.livescience.com/65049-ancient-creature-18-tentacles.html |access-date=2023-06-02 |website=livescience.com |language=en}}</ref> It was a sessile relative to comb jellies.<ref name="bristol-2023a">{{Cite web |last=Bristol |first=University of |title=Half-a-billion-year-old fossil reveals the origins of comb jellies |url=https://phys.org/news/2019-03-half-a-billion-year-old-fossil-reveals-jellies.html |access-date=2023-06-04 |website=phys.org |language=en}}</ref> It had combs with cilia just like modern day comb jellies.<ref name="bristol-2023a" />

It is named after the [[Dai people]]. The name means Dai flower.<ref name="laura-geggel-2019a" />

In 2019, ''Daihua'' and other Cambrian forms were hypothesized to be stem-group [[Ctenophora|ctenophores]]. This leads to the assertion that ctenophores evolved from immotile, suspensivorous forms, a lifestyle similar to that of [[Polyp (zoology)|polyps]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Zhao |first1=Yang |last2=Vinther |first2=Jakob |last3=Parry |first3=Luke A. |last4=Wei |first4=Fan |last5=Green |first5=Emily |last6=Pisani |first6=Davide |last7=Hou |first7=Xianguang |last8=Edgecombe |first8=Gregory D. |last9=Cong |first9=Peiyun |date=2019-04-01 |title=Cambrian Sessile, Suspension Feeding Stem-Group Ctenophores and Evolution of the Comb Jelly Body Plan |journal=Current Biology |language=en |volume=29 |issue=7 |pages=1112–1125.e2 |doi=10.1016/j.cub.2019.02.036 |pmid=30905603 |s2cid=84844387 |issn=0960-9822|doi-access=free |hdl=1983/40a6bcb8-a740-482c-a23c-7d563faea5c5 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> Cladogram after Zhao ''et al.'', 2019:
{{clade|{{clade sequential|Crown [[Cnidaria]]|''[[Xianguangia]]''|'''''Daihua'''''|''[[Dinomischus]]''|''[[Siphusauctum]]''|''[[Galeactena]]''|Crown [[Ctenophora]]}}}}
